summary: This is a fourth revision of a controlled, from-scratch comparison of token-level predictive entropy, semantic entropy, and self-consistency as error-prediction signals on a synthetic arithmetic task. Building on v3 (which showed the token-entropy advantage was directionally consistent across 5 seeds but not uniformly significant per-seed), this version adds three things three separate round-3 reviewers asked for: (1) it leads with the distribution of per-seed p-values (median 0.122 for semantic-vs-token, 0.032 for self-consistency-vs-token) rather than the non-representative seed-0 headline; (2) it applies Holm-Bonferroni correction across all 10 per-seed pairwise tests, finding zero survive at family-wise alpha=0.05; and (3) it stress-tests its own sign test, showing a single seed flip would move p from 0.031 to 0.19. It also fixes the artifact/text runtime mismatch flagged in three round-3 reviews by re-running and re-shipping matched code/data/text (563.2s, matching the shipped results_summary_v2.json's elapsed_seconds=563.19). The paper's conclusion is now a fully corrected null result at the family-wise level, reframed as a case study in escalating statistical rigor across four drafts.
strengths:
- Directly and verifiably resolves my own round-3 objection: I re-checked results_summary_v2.json and elapsed_seconds=563.1880798339844 matches the paper's stated '563.2 seconds' exactly, and run_output.log in the directory shows this is the actual run that produced the shipped JSON (seed-by-seed accuracies and AUROCs in the log match both the JSON and the paper's Table verbatim) — the artifact-drift bug from v3 is genuinely fixed, not just reworded.
- The Holm-Bonferroni correction is correctly computed and reported honestly against the paper's own prior framing: sorted p-values (0.007, 0.021, 0.029, 0.032, 0.036, 0.122, 0.203, 0.264, 0.326, 0.356) against thresholds 0.005, 0.0056, ... correctly shows the smallest p (0.007) fails to clear 0.005, so zero of ten survive — I independently verified this arithmetic and it is correct, and the paper doesn't shy away from the fact that this undercuts its own prior draft's '2/5 and 3/5 significant' framing.
- The median-p-value framing and sign-test fragility check are both substantively new (not just relabeled prior content) and directly address the exact concerns raised across my rounds 2 and 3 reviews (seed-selection sensitivity, whether a single seed's significance is representative); both computations check out against per_seed_bootstrap_tests and seed_win_sign_test in the released JSON.
weaknesses:
- The paper's contribution is now almost entirely methodological/self-referential (four drafts documenting the same experiment's evolving statistical treatment) rather than a substantively new scientific finding about uncertainty signals; the actual open question raised across all four drafts — why token entropy's edge concentrates in 2-3 digit answers and reverses on 1-digit answers — remains unresolved, and future work again defers it rather than investigating with the existing K-sweep-scale effort.
- With the corrected result now an explicit family-wise null (zero of ten tests survive Holm-Bonferroni), the paper's power to detect a true effect at n=5 seeds is very low by construction, and the paper acknowledges this in Limitations but doesn't quantify what seed count would be needed beyond a rough per-seed timing estimate (~110s/seed) — a power calculation would have made the 'not enough evidence' claim more precise rather than qualitative.
- The digit-length stratification (n=37 for 1-digit) is carried over unchanged from v3 with the same caveats (no significance test, no correction) and still is not integrated into the Holm-Bonferroni correction framework the rest of the paper now applies rigorously elsewhere, creating a minor inconsistency in how strictly different parts of Results are held to the same statistical standard the paper otherwise insists on.
questions:
1. Given that the family-wise-corrected result is a null across all 10 tests, and future work proposes more seeds at ~110s/seed, have you run (or can you estimate via a power analysis) how many seeds would be needed to detect the observed effect sizes (e.g., the self-consistency-vs-token median p=0.032) at a Holm-corrected alpha=0.05 with reasonable power?
2. Why wasn't the same Holm-Bonferroni correction standard applied to the digit-length stratification (3 strata x 2 comparisons = 6 additional tests), given the paper now treats multiple-comparison correction as a first-class concern everywhere else?
3. Now that the mechanism question (why token entropy wins on 2-3 digit but not 1-digit answers) has survived four drafts unanswered, do you have a concrete next experiment planned to test it directly (e.g., per-digit-position entropy decomposition) rather than flagging it again as future work?
